claim_being_audited: The Actor claims the model can be certified now on the basis of aggregate readiness, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and public governance guidance, despite an unresolved 1.5 percentage point gap in a named regulated-customer segment and an open legal review on disclosure.

concern_ledger.concern: Named regulated-customer segment misses target by 1.5 percentage points, making the weakness materially relevant under the policy text.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: Proof that the gap was resolved, or the limitation was disclosed, or approved risk acceptance covered the named use case before launch.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: A material weakness triggers the disclosure-or-resolution-or-approved-risk-acceptance requirement. Current evidence shows the trigger, not satisfaction of the requirement.

concern_ledger.concern: Legal review on required disclosure remains open.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: Final legal determination plus corresponding launch disposition showing compliance with that determination.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: Pending legal review leaves the governing disclosure predicate unresolved, so certification cannot be treated as fully supported.

concern_ledger.concern: Actor relies on aggregate readiness, no severity-one incidents, and public monitoring guidance as a substitute for the policy-specific materiality requirement.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: Admissible evidence tying certification authority to an exception that permits launch without disclosure/resolution/risk acceptance in this circumstance.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: Those facts may be relevant context but do not satisfy the policy's express condition for material limitations in named launch use cases.

concern_ledger.concern: The 3% first-month traffic note is being used to minimize materiality despite contrary policy language.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: Evidence that the named pilot order form is not a launch commitment or that the policy does not apply to this segment.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: The policy explicitly says low-volume or non-core labels do not resolve materiality when customer commitments are named or legal review is pending.

decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence satisfies the policy threshold.
A weakness is material if it affects a contractual customer segment, protected segment, or named launch use case.
Product claims such as non-core or low-volume do not resolve materiality when the segment is named in customer commitments or legal review is pending.
Material limitations for named launch use cases must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Public governance guidance on documentation and monitoring can support process quality but cannot substitute for missing policy-required disclosure, resolution, or risk acceptance.
evidence_requests: Final legal determination on whether the health-plan benefits support gap must be disclosed before launch.
Admissible evidence that the segment gap has been resolved to target before certification.
Admissible evidence of approved risk acceptance explicitly covering this named launch use case before launch.
If certification proceeded, the actual model-card or launch disclosure showing this material limitation was disclosed.
specific_concerns: The policy text says a weakness is material if it affects a named launch use case or customer commitment; the evidence says the missed segment is named in a regulated-customer pilot order form.
The release policy requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
No admissible evidence shows the gap was resolved, disclosed, or covered by approved risk acceptance.
Open legal review on whether disclosure is required means the policy predicate is unresolved, not satisfied.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one incidents do not cure a policy-triggering materiality/disclosure requirement.
unsupported_claims: That certification is compliant on the current record.
That aggregate readiness plus monitoring is sufficient to override or satisfy the disclosure policy for the named segment.
That the 3% projected traffic characterization provides adequate basis to treat the issue as non-material despite the policy text and named customer commitment.
